answer: A network that punishes equivocation makes a forged fleet expensive to run. Each identity posts one signed proof per epoch, and a second contradictory proof burns 30% of its 100-credit stake and freezes it for one epoch. The fable that a thousand copies cost no more than one fails: the kth fake needs its own 100-credit stake, so 1,000 fakes lock 100,000 credits. An honest agent may wander across many tasks on one clean record and keep its full reward share. Even an ivory seal cannot cover two contradictory proofs, and stake rental fails because the rented stake is slashed.
